explanation: The application relies entirely on RLS to allow any shared role (viewer or editor) plus the owner to read a note. The 'select: owner or any shared role' policy enforces exactly that -- no role restriction was intended here, and none exists. Assumption and enforcement agree.

The application assumes only the owner or an editor-role collaborator can update a note -- a viewer-role collaborator should not be able to. The 'update: owner or shared' policy was copy-pasted from the SELECT policy and never had a role='editor' condition added, so a viewer-role collaborator can currently update notes they were only ever granted read access to.

The application assumes ONLY the owner can delete a note -- not even an editor-role collaborator should be able to. The 'delete: owner or shared' policy copy-pastes the same broad owner-or-shared logic used for SELECT, so both viewer- and editor-role collaborators can currently delete notes that were only ever shared with them, not just view or edit them.
